findings.description: The reports_archive bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration block (and no separate encryption resource), so stored report objects are not encrypted with the customer-managed KMS key used by the audit bucket; encryption depends entirely on account defaults rather than bucket configuration.
The ledger_exports bucket, which holds financial ledger exports, defines no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so there is no enforced encryption of stored data.
The model_artifacts bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so model artifacts are not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key despite versioning and logging being enabled.
The ops_runbooks bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so operational runbook content is stored without enforced encryption at rest.

The seed object uploaded into reports_archive specifies no kms_key_id and no server_side_encryption, and because the target bucket also has no default encryption configuration, the vendor roster object is written without enforced encryption at rest.

The audit trail bucket uses acl = 'log-delivery-write', granting the S3 log delivery group WRITE and READ_ACP on the bucket that holds tamper-evident audit logs, and no bucket policy further scopes that access.
